“Our performance is insane. And we've secured over 50% of long-term contracts through 2028.  

And practically speaking, DRAM and HBM supply is sold out through 2029.  

And right now, demand is overflowing, so if you're worried about any potential demand drop, no need to fret—it's not just Big Tech, but every country around the world is trying to build AI. That demand is massive.  

And you're worried that expanding capacity means supply will ramp up? Because of high-value products like HBM, the process gets way more complex, making it hard to increase supply.  

And fuck, have we gotten burned by Big Tech just once or twice? We don't expand capacity right away just because you say you need it—we tear apart your financial statements first before ramping up. Don't get caught bullshitting.  

And the HBM4 you're worried about? Yields are coming in better than planned, so we've raised targets and shipments start in Q4.  

HBM4E? We already sent samples in Q2 and it's progressing smoothly.  

Reduced stacking defects? We had to cut stacking defects to at least increase the insufficient supply somehow. 

 And 4F²? Please, get a basic grasp of the concepts of tech implementation and commercialization before you start talking”

H/T Polaris log 😂
